$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-yjs-engine-fixtures.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
$description: Deterministic multi-doc scripts with a per-step oracle for the engine doc. The C# test owns ONLY the doc named by `engine` (pin its client id to docs[engine]); every other doc is a recording. A step is one of: "op" (a peer writes; `update` is the bytes it produced, `deliver` the docs that got them at once), "engineWrites" (the ENGINE performs `op` locally and delivers ITS OWN bytes — `update` is only the mirror's copy), "deliver" (a delayed or duplicate delivery of the update produced by step `updateOf`; substitute the engine's own bytes when that step was an engineWrites), and "expect" (assert `sv`, `hasPending` and `json` on the engine doc). Update bytes need not match yjs byte-for-byte, but `sv` and `json` must. A case with `compare: "segments"` has remote formatting, which yjs cleans up after the transaction and the engine does not: compare only `json`, with every Y.Text delta merged into runs of equal attributes, and skip engine bytes and `sv`. Nested $ymap/$yarray/$ytext values integrate the container item first and then their entries in listed order — get that order wrong and the state vector diverges. The fuzz seed files use this same op grammar with two step shortcuts of their own, which each of them states in its own $description.

ops.map.set: root/rootKind/path address a Y.Map; set `key` to `value`
ops.text.insert: insert `text` at `index` (optional `attributes`; absent means inherit the marks in force)

values: JSON, except objects carrying one of $num/$bigint/$u8/$undefined (leaves) or $ymap/$yarray/$ytext/$yxmlfragment/$yxmlelement/$yxmltext (shared types). A $yxmltext may carry `ops`: text ops (no root/path) written while it is not in a doc yet, replayed in order.

cases.name: concurrent-map-set-two-clients
cases.description: Two clients set the same key with no knowledge of each other; last-writer-wins is decided by client id, not arrival order.

cases.name: concurrent-map-set-three-clients
cases.description: Three clients — including the engine — set the same key concurrently.

cases.name: concurrent-array-insert-three-clients
cases.description: Three clients insert at index 0 of the same empty array: pure YATA ordering.

cases.name: out-of-order-delivery
cases.description: Three sequential ops from one client delivered 3, 1, 2: the receiver parks pending until the gap closes.

cases.name: duplicate-delivery
cases.description: The same update delivered three times is idempotent.

cases.name: delete-concurrent-with-insert-in-run
cases.description: A deletes the middle of a four-item run while B inserts into it: integration must split the run at a clean start and a clean end.

cases.name: pending-delete-set
cases.description: Only the deletion reaches the receiver; its delete set names clocks the receiver has never seen (pendingDs).

cases.name: delete-set-only-update
cases.description: Once the insert is known, the deletion travels as an update with zero struct groups and a non-empty delete set.

cases.name: delete-then-reinsert-key
cases.description: Set, delete, set again on one key.

cases.name: cascade-delete-grid
cases.description: Deleting a block whose data holds a grid deletes every descendant; with gc on, the children become GC structs.

cases.name: cascade-delete-grid-no-gc
cases.description: The same cascade in a gc: false world, pinning the encoding where the deleted children survive as ContentType.

cases.name: nul-and-astral-strings
cases.description: NUL is ordinary data in keys, values and text; astral characters are two UTF-16 code units.

cases.name: array-run-split-by-remote-insert
cases.description: A five-string run from one client, split by a remote insert into its middle.

cases.name: text-format-and-embed
cases.description: A Y.Text root carrying formats and an embed, with the engine performing the minimal insert/delete API around them.

cases.name: formatted-text-engine-writes
cases.description: The engine writes every formatted-text op into a fresh Y.XmlText: inserts with attributes, format add and remove, an object-valued mark, embeds with and without attributes, a delete across marks, and a format that runs past the end.

cases.name: formatted-text-prelim-queue
cases.description: Writes on a Y.XmlText that is not in a doc yet are queued and replayed in order when it integrates.

cases.name: formatted-text-link-key-order
cases.description: A peer links "ab" with {href, rel}; the engine types right after it with {rel, href}. yjs compares object marks flat and key-order-free, so it writes no format item.

cases.name: formatted-text-equal-links-cleanup
cases.description: Deleting the plain gap between two equal but distinct link marks keeps both: yjs cleanupFormattingGap compares with ===, which is reference identity for objects.

cases.name: formatted-text-remote-overlap
cases.description: Two peers bold overlapping ranges concurrently. The receiving yjs doc runs its format cleanup, the engine does not (contract section 7), so only canonical segments are comparable: see `compare`.

cases.name: engine-writes-while-pending
cases.description: The edit-API path: the engine writes locally while it still holds a parked struct, so its own diff has to interleave local structs with pending ones.

cases.name: foreign-values-from-a-peer
cases.description: Values the engine decodes and re-encodes but never authors itself: a bigint, a Uint8Array and undefined.
